items.title: Scott Yanow interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 22, 2021
items.q: You know Garry Giddins is great, you know he’s my generation. He and Francis Davis, you know, I rate them both very high.

ctx.x: In the older days, say oh 1970 or so, there were less recordings coming out and there were less reviews to write. But then again you had some really tremendous writers, you know, some of the ones who I read when I was starting out were just great. And they all had their faults and their good points, but I mean my early heroes were Leonard Feather because he was so dominant during that era, even though you know he’s not perfect and there are certain things — I could talk about him for an hour. Leonard Feather, Nat…

giants. We now have a lot more writers I think but there’s no one that dominates the field. You know Garry Giddins is great, you know he’s my generation. He and Francis Davis, you know, I rate them both very high. The current writers, also are quite good, I just can’t think of any one that I would pick out and see oh he’s the best one or she’s the best one right now.

What about the — every few years there is a controversy or at least a debate is raised about who owns jazz. Is jazz an African-American art form or is it — what happened to the white innovators? Have you ever gotten in the middle of that subject matter?
